question: Under the POCSO Act 2012, a doctor who becomes aware of sexual abuse of a person under 18 years of age is legally obligated to report it to the police, regardless of the patient's or parents' wishes.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. POCSO Act 2012 Section 19 mandates that ANY person who knows or reasonably suspects a sexual offence against a child MUST report to the Special Juvenile Police Unit or local police. The doctor cannot withhold this report even if the adolescent requests confidentiality — confidentiality has this specific, legislated exception.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Section 19 of the POCSO Act 2012 imposes a mandatory reporting obligation on every person, including healthcare providers, who has knowledge that a sexual offence has been committed against a child (under 18). Failure to report is a punishable offence under Section 21. Confidentiality cannot override this statutory duty.
